Dissona MCP server.

Audio policy (FR-009): audio descriptors returned by dissona_get_chapter_audio_info are listen URLs. The LLM cannot autonomously play audio — there is no 'listen' tool by design. Forward the URL to the user or to a downstream audio player.

## github
The GitHub MCP Server provides tools to interact with GitHub platform.

Tool selection guidance:
	1. Use 'list_*' tools for broad, simple retrieval and pagination of all items of a type (e.g., all issues, all PRs, all branches) with basic filtering.
	2. Use 'search_*' tools for targeted queries with specific criteria, keywords, or complex filters (e.g., issues with certain text, PRs by author, code containing functions).

Context management:
	1. Use pagination whenever possible with batches of 5-10 items.
	2. Use minimal_output parameter set to true if the full information is not needed to accomplish a task.

Tool usage guidance:
	1. For 'search_*' tools: Use separate 'sort' and 'order' parameters if available for sorting results - do not include 'sort:' syntax in query strings. Query strings should contain only search criteria (e.g., 'org:google language:python'), not sorting instructions. Always call 'get_me' first to understand current user permissions and context. ## Issues

Check 'list_issue_types' first for organizations to use proper issue types. Use 'search_issues' before creating new issues to avoid duplicates. Always set 'state_reason' when closing issues. ## Pull Requests

PR review workflow: Always use 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'create' to create a pending review, then 'add_comment_to_pending_review' to add comments, and finally 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'submit_pending' to submit the review for complex reviews with line-specific comments.

Before creating a pull request, search for pull request templates in the repository. Template files are called pull_request_template.md or they're located in '.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE' directory. Use the template content to structure the PR description and then call create_pull_request tool.

aiTitle: Configure Claude Code to load global skills

content.text:
Based on my research of the official Claude Code documentation, here's what I found:

## 1. Default Skill Locations

Claude Code loads skills from these locations (in priority order):

| Location | Path | Scope |
|----------|------|-------|
| **Personal** | `~/.claude/skills/` | All your projects |
| **Project** | `.claude/skills/` | Current repo only |
| **Parent directories** | `../../../.claude/skills/` | Up to repo root |
| **Nested directories** | `./packages/*/.claude/skills/` | Discovered when accessing those files |
| **Enterprise/Plugins** | Via managed settings or plugins | Organization-wide |

**Reference:** [Extend Claude with skills - Where skills live](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills.md)

---

## 2. Custom Skills Path Options

Unfortunately, **there is no native `skillDirectories` configuration key** to specify arbitrary paths like `~/.agents/skills`. However, you have these alternatives:

### **Option A: Use `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` (Simplest)**
Set this environment variable to redirect the entire `~/.claude` directory to another location:

```bash
export CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=~/.agents
# Now Claude Code loads skills from ~/.agents/skills/ automatically
```

This also redirects all other `~/.claude` configuration (CLAUDE.md, settings.json, plugins, etc.) to `~/.agents/`.

**Reference:** [Extend Claude with skills - Live change detection](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills.md)

---

### **Option B: Use `--add-dir` Flag (Partial)**
Load skills from an additional directory at session start:

```bash
claude --add-dir ~/.agents
# Loads skills from ~/.agents/.claude/skills/ automatically
```

The skills must be nested under `.claude/skills/` within the added directory. This grants file access AND loads skills from that subdirectory.

**Reference:** [Skills from additional directories](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills.md)

---

### **Option C: Symlink (Most Flexible)**
Link individual skills from `~/.agents/skills` into `~/.claude/skills`:

```bash
# Example: link a single skill
ln -s ~/.agents/skills/deep-research ~/.claude/skills/deep-research

# Or symlink the entire directory
ln -s ~/.agents/skills ~/.claude/skills/global-skills
# Then invoke via /global-skills:deep-research
```

Symlinks work at the enterprise, personal, and project levels.

**Reference:** [Where skills live - Symlinks](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills.md)

---

## Recommendation

For a global skills directory at `~/.agents/skills`, I recommend:

1. **Best: Use `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`** if you want all personal config (`~/.claude/`) to live under `~/.agents/`.  
   Add to your shell profile: `export CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=~/.agents`

2. **Fallback: Use `--add-dir ~/.agents`** if you want to keep `~/.claude/` separate but load additional skills.  
   Add to your shell profile: `alias claude='claude --add-dir ~/.agents'`

3. **Manual: Use symlinks** if you only want specific skills from `~/.agents/skills` available.

---

**Official Sources:**
- [Extend Claude with skills - Where skills live](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills.md)
- [Live change detection & discovery from additional directories](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills.md)
- [Claude Code settings configuration](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/settings.md)

---

```bash

# Or symlink the entire directory

```

---

## Recommendation

For a global skills directory at `~/.agents/skills`, I recommend:

1. **Best: Use `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`** if you want all personal config (`~/.claude/`) to live under `~/.agents/`.  
   Add to your shell profile: `export CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=~/.agents`

2. **Fallback: Use `--add-dir ~/.agents`** if you want to keep `~/.claude/` separate but load additional skills.  
   Add to your shell profile: `alias claude='claude --add-dir ~/.agents'`

3. **Manual: Use symlinks** if you only want specific skills from `~/.agents/skills` available.

---

**Official Sources:**
- [Extend Claude with skills - Where skills live](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills.md)
- [Live change detection & discovery from additional directories](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills.md)
- [Claude Code settings configuration](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/settings.md)

Short answer: there's **no native "custom skills path" setting** — Claude Code always discovers skills from `~/.claude/skills/` (personal) and `.claude/skills/` (project) plus plugins. You can't just point a `skillDirectories` key at `~/.agents/skills`. But there are three ways to get skills from `~/.agents/skills` loaded:

## Option A — Move all config there with `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`
```bash
export CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=~/.agents
```
Then Claude Code reads skills from `~/.agents/skills/` automatically. Caveat: this redirects **everything** (`settings.json`, `CLAUDE.md`, plugins, projects, credentials…) into `~/.agents/`, not just skills. Only do this if you want the whole `~/.claude` tree to live under `~/.agents`.

## Option B — Symlink (most targeted, best fit for a dotfiles setup)
Keep `~/.claude` as-is and just link your global skills in:
```bash
# whole directory as a namespace (invoke as /global:<skill>)
ln -s ~/.agents/skills ~/.claude/skills/global

# or individual skills at top level
ln -s ~/.agents/skills/my-skill ~/.claude/skills/my-skill
```
Claude Code follows symlinks, so the skills show up as normal personal skills.

## Option C — `--add-dir` per session
```bash
claude --add-dir ~/.agents
```
This loads skills nested under `~/.agents/.claude/skills/` (note the `.claude/` layer) — so it only works if your skills live at `~/.agents/.claude/skills/`, not directly at `~/.agents/skills/`. Works via a shell alias but is more awkward than the symlink.

---

**My recommendation:** since you manage a Nix dotfiles repo, go with **Option B (symlink)**. It's declarative-friendly (you can create the symlink via `home.file` / `home.activation` in home-manager), keeps `~/.claude` intact, and doesn't drag the rest of your config into `~/.agents`. Something like:

```nix
home.file.".claude/skills/global".source =
  config.lib.file.mkOutOfStoreSymlink "${config.home.homeDirectory}/.agents/skills";
```

Want me to wire that symlink into your home-manager config?

Sources: [Claude Code Skills docs](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills.md), [settings](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/settings.md).
